title: the WSG ultravision and infravision effectiveness slice - the heat-as-light color scale with the temperature bands, the surface-temperature perception rules, heat blindness and the cold-blooded bar, and the ultravision definition with its five range modifiers, printed p. 74
audit_comment: The ultravision and infravision effectiveness rules: infravision is useless in daylight or under artificial illumination stronger than moonlight, the normally visible light overriding the heat radiation. A character using infravision sees heat as light - very cold objects very dark, hot objects very bright, temperatures between the two as varying shades of gray - with the color of objects classified on a scale from 1 (pitch black, below -50) to 10 (excruciatingly bright, above 130), the interior bands -50 to -11, -10 to 15, 16 to 32, 33 to 50, 51 to 70, 71 to 90, 91 to 110 and 111 to 130 each contiguous with its neighbors. The air temperature dictates the overall brightness; a surface temperature warmer or colder than the air shows as a brighter or darker image. A human (body temperature approximately 98 degrees) in normal clothing appears brighter than his surroundings when the air is 90 or lower, as do demi-humans and most size M humanoids; a human bundled in heavy clothing matches the air and is undetectable, save small uncovered spots of brightness - or darkness in very hot air. Obstruction blocks detection as with normal vision, but a great source of heat or cold may be indirectly detectable through the air it warms: a campfire behind a large rock shows the rock's near side as a dark shape against a lighter background. Extreme heat or cold with everything at one temperature renders infravision useless - below -50 all pitch black, above 130 a blanket of almost blinding brightness - and sudden close proximity to great heat (a wall of fire) inflicts heat blindness, burning the power out until cure blindness, or temporarily blinding to infrared rays for 5-10 turns (1d6+4). Cold-blooded creatures (reptiles, insects, most nonmammalians) are undetectable at air temperature, but magic that abruptly changes the air temperature reveals them briefly. Ultravision, or night vision, sees into the ultraviolet range, distinguishing colors, shapes and relative positions even in darkness; only the deep gnome has it inborn, night vision to 30 yards as if by normal vision in daylight; others gain it temporarily by magic (lens of ultravision, the magic-user or illusionist ultravision spell), capabilities varying by means. It is useless under any light brighter than moonlight - daylight or artificial illumination yields nothing but blackness - and works best on a moonless night under a clear sky: partly cloudy x 2/3, overcast x 1/2, moonlight partly cloudy x 1/3, moonlight overcast x 1/4, viewer under thick cover x 1/4, the last cumulative - a thick forest on a moonlit overcast night leaves only 1/16 of the ideal range.

banner.title: R484: the WSG ULTRAVISION and infravision effectiveness slice, printed p. 74 - the third vision-and-visibility round, a prose round with a pin-table interior (no printed grid): the infravision daylight bar, the heat-as-light color scale with its ten temperature bands, the surface-temperature perception examples, the obstruction and campfire rules, the extreme-climate and heat-blindness rules with the 1d6+4 recovery, the cold-blooded bar, and the ultravision definition with the deep gnome 30-yard range, the brighter-than-moonlight bar, and the five sky-condition range modifiers.
banner.provenance: The settle: the ten temperature bands, the 98/90 human example, the 5-10 turn (1d6+4) recovery, the deep gnome 30 yards and the 1/16 forest example read two-way clean (tesseract, pdfy and tsv agree on every number). The five sky-condition fractions were CONTESTED - both text readers garbled the fraction slashes (tesseract X 2/5, X 2, X s, X /s, X s; pdfy X 2/3, x 112, x 113, X 114, X 114) - and took six vision reads to settle: the tiny stacked numerals repeatedly pattern-completed to 1/2 on line one, but the first full-list read, the pdfy text layer (X 2/3 with a real slash) and an independent published transcription of the WSG list all agree on the descending ladder 2/3, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/4, and the book's own worked example (moonlit overcast x thick cover = 1/16) independently confirms both 1/4 entries. The artificial illumination section opens at the page bottom and is cut mid-word - it stays out of scope for the R485 round.
banner.sentinel: Bounds held: the ten color bands tile the scale with no gaps (each interior low is exactly one above the previous high), the recovery dice 1d6+4 spans exactly 5-10, and the five modifiers descend 2/3, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 with thick cover cumulative into the 1/16 forest floor.

consts.name: wuvColorScaleMin
consts.comment: the infravisual color scale runs from 1

consts.name: wuvBand2Low
consts.comment: color 2: -50 to -11 (the very-cold floor is below -50)

consts.name: wuvBrightBelowAirF
consts.comment: a normally clothed human appears brighter than his surroundings when the air temperature is 90 or lower

consts.name: wuvTempBlindMinTurns
consts.comment: temporary infrared blindness lasts at least 5 turns

consts.name: wuvDeepGnomeRangeYards
consts.comment: the deep gnome has inborn night vision to a range of 30 yards

consts.name: wuvMoonlessCloudyNum
consts.comment: moonless night partly cloudy: x 2/3, numerator

consts.name: wuvThickCoverNum
consts.comment: viewer standing under thick cover: x 1/4, numerator

consts.name: wuvForestExampleNum
consts.comment: the worked example: thick forest on a moonlit overcast night = 1/16 of ideal range

bools.name: wuvUselessInDaylight
bools.comment: infravision is useless in daylight or when the viewer or the target is bathed in artificial illumination stronger than moonlight

bools.name: wuvVisibleLightOverrides
bools.comment: in such cases the normally visible light overrides the heat radiation, and the former is all that can be sensed

bools.name: wuvSeesHeatAsLight
bools.comment: a character using infravision sees heat as light

bools.name: wuvColdDarkHotBright
bools.comment: very cold objects are very dark, hot objects are very bright, and temperatures between the extremes are varying shades of gray

bools.name: wuvScale1PitchBlack
bools.comment: color 1 on the scale is pitch black

bools.name: wuvScale10Excruciating
bools.comment: color 10 on the scale is excruciatingly bright

bools.name: wuvAirTempDictates
bools.comment: the first thing to consider is the temperature of the air, which dictates the overall level of brightness perceived

bools.name: wuvWarmerColderShows
bools.comment: an object or creature with a surface temperature warmer or colder than the air appears as a brighter or darker image against the backdrop of the atmosphere

bools.name: wuvHumanBrightAt90OrBelow
bools.comment: a human in nothing thicker than normal clothing appears brighter than his surroundings when the air temperature is 90 or lower

bools.name: wuvDemiHumanSameRule
bools.comment: the same holds true for demi-humans and most size M humanoids with roughly human body temperatures

bools.name: wuvBundledUndetectable
bools.comment: a human completely bundled in heavy clothing has the same surface temperature as the surrounding air and is not detectable by infravision

bools.name: wuvUncoveredSpotsShow
bools.comment: if just a small part of the body (such as the face or hands) is uncovered, those areas appear as small spots of brightness

bools.name: wuvUncoveredDarkIfHot
bools.comment: or of darkness, if the air temperature is very high

bools.name: wuvObstructionBlocks
bools.comment: in most cases infravision will not detect an object or creature when the line of sight is obstructed - a man crouched behind a large rock is invisible, just as to normal vision

bools.name: wuvStrongHeatIndirect
bools.comment: an object or creature giving off a great amount of heat or cold might be indirectly detectable because its presence changes the temperature of the surrounding air

bools.name: wuvCampfireRockExample
bools.comment: a campfire built behind a large rock warms the air, and the side of the rock facing the viewer appears as a dark shape outlined against a lighter background

bools.name: wuvExtremeSameTempUseless
bools.comment: extreme heat or extreme cold renders infravision useless when everything in the range of vision is effectively at the same temperature

bools.name: wuvVeryColdPitchBlack
bools.comment: in a very cold climate, temperature lower than -50 degrees, everything appears pitch black

bools.name: wuvVeryHotBlinding
bools.comment: in a very hot climate, temperature higher than 130, infravision detects nothing but a blanket of almost blinding brightness

bools.name: wuvHeatBlindnessRisk
bools.comment: a character using infravision can be afflicted by heat blindness if he suddenly finds himself in close proximity to a large fire or a source of great heat

bools.name: wuvWallOfFireBurnout
bools.comment: a wall of fire springing up in front of an infraviewer burns out his infravision and renders the power useless until cure blindness or similar healing magic is applied

bools.name: wuvTempBlindRecover
bools.comment: in a less extreme case the viewer is only temporarily blinded to infrared rays while his eyes recover from the shock

bools.name: wuvColdBloodedUndetected
bools.comment: infravision will not detect cold-blooded creatures (reptiles, insects, and most other nonmammalian creatures) because their temperature is the same as that of the surrounding air

bools.name: wuvMagicTempReveals
bools.comment: if magic abruptly changes the temperature of the surrounding air, a cold-blooded creature stands out against the background for a short time because its body temperature does not change that quickly

bools.name: wuvNightVisionDefinition
bools.comment: ultravision, or night vision, is the ability to see into the ultraviolet range of the spectrum and thereby distinguish objects from their surroundings even in darkness

bools.name: wuvDarknessRedefined
bools.comment: for an ultraviewer the word darkness takes on a different meaning: he can distinguish colors, shapes, and the relative position of objects even in the absence of light in the normal visible spectrum

bools.name: wuvDeepGnomeOnly
bools.comment: only one character race, the deep gnome, has inborn ultravisual capabilities

bools.name: wuvDeepGnomeDaylightQuality
bools.comment: objects within the deep gnome's night vision range are visible to him just as if he was using normal vision during daylight

bools.name: wuvMagicalAcquisition
bools.comment: other characters can acquire ultravision temporarily through magical means, such as a lens of ultravision and the ultravision spell, cast by a magic-user or an illusionist

bools.name: wuvMagicalCapabilitiesVary
bools.comment: the exact capabilities bestowed by magical ultravision (range and amount of illumination perceived) vary depending on the means employed

bools.name: wuvUltraUselessInLight
bools.comment: as with infravision, ultravision is useless when the viewer or the target is illuminated by any light source brighter than moonlight

bools.name: wuvUltraDaylightBlackness
bools.comment: a character trying to use ultravision in daylight or in an area affected by artificial illumination sees nothing but blackness

bools.name: wuvBestMoonlessClear
bools.comment: ultravision works best during a moonless night under a clear sky

bools.name: wuvThickCoverCumulative
bools.comment: the thick-cover modifier is cumulative with any other modifier that applies
